citation: Wong G, Clegg ME, Ross D, et al. Sequential Meals Containing Animal and Plant-Based Saturated Fats Have Differential Effects on Postprandial Gut Hormones but No Impact on Satiety Compared with Unsaturated Fats in Generally Healthy Males: Findings from the Randomized Controlled Crossover CocoHeart Study☆. The Journal of Nutrition. 2025;155(9):3020-3029.
protocol: Sequential high-fat meals: breakfast at 0 min (toasted white bread, jam, chocolate drink; 50 g test fat, 53.6 g total fat) and lunch at 330 min (30 g test fat, 33.6 g total fat); test fat butter, coconut oil or a vegetable-oil blend; crossover. Blood at -30, 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300, 330, 360, 390, 420, 480 min.
population: 13 generally healthy Caucasian men; age 53 ± 3 y; BMI 24.4 ± 0.8 kg/m2; UK (Reading).

reports.where: Table 4: AUC over 480 min and other summary measures per fat

note: Middle-aged men over two consecutive fat-rich meals, with incretins in the same table. Same lab and design family as almoraie-2026 but a different population. Insulin units look odd (ng/L and µg/L × 480 min), so the reader must check them. Only in figures: time courses. Meal kinds: fat load, mixed meal.
